monthly_review.summary: This month shows a deliberate shift toward lower-intensity, higher-volume aerobic development — evidenced by increased Z1 time, reduced average HR, and slightly slower average pace — while maintaining VO2 max and improving running efficiency metrics.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone 1 time jumped from 23% to 39% while Zone 4+ dropped from 19% to 1%, indicating a strategic de-emphasis on threshold work in favor of foundational aerobic volume.

goal_tracker.message: You need 0.2 more km across 1 session to match last month’s distance — easily achievable with a short 2–3 km easy run before month-end.

insights.title: Efficiency dip despite cadence gain
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency declined from 13.66 to 13.39 m/sec per bpm this month, even as cadence rose from 142 to 145 spm — suggesting stride length or ground contact time adjustments may be limiting efficiency gains.

insights.title: Strong aerobic base emphasis
insights.body: Z1+Z2 time now accounts for 83% of total HR time (vs 55% last month), with Z4/Z5 nearly eliminated (1% vs 19%) — a clear, intentional shift toward low-intensity endurance development.

insights.title: Improved form under fatigue
insights.body: On the 2.5 km run at 7:27/min/km (447 sec/km, best pace), stride length increased to 94.35 cm and ground contact dropped to 286 ms — showing efficient mechanics at faster effort despite modest weekly volume.

insights.title: Reduced acute load but stable VO2 max
insights.body: Average aerobic TE fell from 3.1 to 2.7, yet VO2 max remains steady at 37.0 — confirming that lower-intensity volume is sustaining aerobic capacity without excessive stress.

recommendations.action: Do one 5 km Zone 2 run at avg HR ≤135 bpm before May 31st, focusing on holding cadence ≥148 spm and stride length ≥72 cm.
recommendations.reason: Your recent Zone 2 runs show cadence and stride variability (e.g., 5.5 km run: 149 spm / 69.7 cm; 5.6 km run: 151 spm / 67.6 cm) — consistency here will reinforce aerobic efficiency gains.

recommendations.action: Add one 10-minute post-run drill routine (A-skips, butt kicks, high knees) after your next easy run to reinforce neuromuscular coordination at 148–150 spm.
recommendations.reason: Cadence improved +3 spm this month but vertical oscillation rose slightly (7.5 → 7.7 cm avg), suggesting economy gains are not yet fully integrated — drills can help refine turnover quality.

recommendations.action: Repeat your 2.5 km fast run (May 16) as a benchmark: aim for same pace (447 sec/km) but target ground contact ≤285 ms and vertical oscillation ≤7.6 cm.
recommendations.reason: That session achieved your best pace *and* lowest ground contact (286 ms) — replicating it will test whether you can sustain that efficiency under similar effort.

weekly_focus.description: Prioritize rhythm, repeatability, and form awareness at Zone 2 intensities — using cadence, ground contact, and vertical oscillation as real-time feedback levers.
suggested_sessions: 5 km Zone 2 run (HR ≤135 bpm, cadence ≥148 spm)
2.5 km paced run at 447 sec/km with focus on ground contact
